taxonomic_note: Accepted as a species by major current authorities, but Texas native status is unresolved: POWO treats Texas as introduced while USDA GRIN and Flora of North America support native/southwestern-U.S. treatment.
look_here_first: Separate it from Euphorbia dentata with mature seed/capsule and leaf-hair texture: E. davidii tends to have larger capsules and seeds, angular irregularly tuberculate seeds, and shorter stiffer hairs with small pustular bases.

project_inclusion.target_zone_status: AUTHORITY CONFLICT — USER APPROVED LEARNER INCLUSION
project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO treats Texas as introduced; USDA GRIN explicitly treats Texas as native, and FNA describes a native southwestern U.S./northern Mexico to southern Great Plains range. The project does not manufacture PASS or FAIL while that conflict remains.

approval_exception.reason: Learner inclusion is allowed while authority conflict remains explicit.

best_field_traits: short stout abaxial hairs often on minute pustular bases
broadly ovoid capsules larger than in E. dentata
larger angular seeds with irregular low tubercles or wrinkles
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Use seed shape/size, capsule size, and hair texture against E. dentata. Habit alone is unreliable.

comparisons.key_distinctions: E. davidii generally has larger capsules and angular unevenly tuberculate seeds plus shorter stiffer pustule-based hairs; E. dentata has smaller, more rounded and evenly pebbled seeds with weaker filiform hairs.

photo_note: Seed and leaf-hair macros remain the highest-value diagnostic visual additions.
